findings.title: APT-2026-11-01 security update
findings.summary_md: The APT maintainers announced security updates covering CVE-2026-109518, a critical file verification bypass. A remote attacker could bypass verification of downloaded packages using redirects and transient HTTP server errors that cause APT to retry downloads, letting APT override existing hardlinks with a chosen payload; because .deb files install as root, this enables remote code execution. The issue relies on Acquire::Retries being set, which has been the default since APT 2.3.2, though many user scripts may have used it in older releases. The report is credited to Max Justicz.

findings.title: [SECURITY] [DSA 6607-1] apt security update
findings.summary_md: Debian Security Advisory DSA-6607-1, issued by Salvatore Bonaccorso on November 4, 2026, fixes CVE-2026-109518 in apt. Max Justicz discovered that APT can merge two different package downloads after an HTTP redirect gives them the same URI, and improper file handling when resuming an HTTP download lets a man-in-the-middle attacker replace a package after verification, resulting in arbitrary code execution as root. For the stable distribution (trixie) the problem is fixed in apt 3.0.4, and the update also addresses several out-of-bounds access issues.

findings.title: [SECURITY] [DLA 4880-1] apt security update
findings.summary_md: Debian LTS Advisory DLA-4880-1 fixes CVE-2026-109518 in apt for Debian 12 (bookworm), in version 2.6.2. Max Justicz discovered that APT can merge two package downloads after an HTTP redirect gives them the same URI, allowing a man-in-the-middle attacker to replace a verified package and execute arbitrary code as root. The update also addresses several out-of-bounds access issues.

findings.title: Debian patches APT flaw that let attackers swap packages after verification
findings.summary_md: Debian published security advisory DSA-6607-1 on November 4, 2026, patching CVE-2026-109518 in the APT package manager, discovered by Max Justicz. The bug lets APT merge two different package downloads after an HTTP redirect gives them the same URI, so a man-in-the-middle attacker can swap the file on disk after APT has already verified it, installing and executing arbitrary code as root. The fix ships in apt 3.0.4 for trixie and the advisory also notes several out-of-bounds access fixes.

findings.title: Debian patches APT flaw that let network attackers swap verified packages for root code
findings.summary_md: RuntimeWire reports that Debian published DSA-6607-1 on November 4, 2026, fixing CVE-2026-109518 in APT, a flaw discovered by Max Justicz. A man-in-the-middle attacker can replace a verified package and execute arbitrary code as root by abusing APT's handling of resumed HTTP downloads and redirects. The fix ships in APT 3.0.4 for trixie.

findings.title: Debian and Ubuntu APT Flaw Lets MitM Attackers Swap Verified Packages and Run Code as Root
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News reports that APT flaw CVE-2026-109518 lets attackers with HTTP traffic control replace verified packages and execute code as root when downloads retry. Debian issued DSA-6607-1 and Ubuntu issued USN-8996-1 on November 4, 2026; Max Justicz reported the flaw. None of the advisory reports describe attacks exploiting the flaw or offer a workaround for systems that cannot update yet.
